then.text: Mind the cranes on your way out. Samson's in a mood. Goliath's fine, but he's the quiet sort.
Keep the lantern lit up north. Folk say the Highlands are bonny. They are. They're also very, very dark.
Sparks are flying and the cranes are quiet. If you've a mind for it, my lot could do with a proper test.

else.text: Once a day, mate. Metal needs to cool or it cracks. Come tomorrow.
Another time, then. The offer stands.
A shipyard shed with a roof like a cathedral and a floor you could eat your dinner off, if you didn't mind the sparks. A figure in a welding visor flips it up.
You'll be the one who's been tidying up after the Enclosure all over the islands. Grand. Welcome to the yard.
They built ships here you could see from space, near enough. Iron creatures are the same. Slow to start, impossible to stop.
Don't mind the noise. It's only the apprentices. They think a rivet is a personality. Let's see what you've got.
The Iron Stone. It held up a ship or two in its day. It holds a team together the same way: not clever, only very hard to knock over.
{player} received the Iron Stone!
And the lantern, as promised. Off the hook by the door. It's older than I am and twice as reliable.
Here's the thing about iron. It remembers every furnace it's been through. With the Stone in your pocket, you can see in a dark cave. Carry the Lantern and the way out will always find you.
There's a cave or two up in Scotland that'll want it. Go on, away. And mind the gulls on the quay. They'll have your chips.
Your phone buzzes. Professor Garside, who sounds as if she is eating a scone over a map.
{player}! The Iron Stone! Eight! I've run out of fingers and started on the biscuits.
The ferry from Belfast will take you across the North Channel to Cairnryan now. The sailors have had a word with the harbour, and the harbour has had a word with the tide.
Scotland has a new Regional Director for the Enclosure. A Morag Strachan. Waxed jacket, clipboard, wellies, and by all accounts a will of iron. You'll get on.
But the Causeway first, if you like. Vane's been spotted at the Giant's Causeway with a marquee. Don't ask me how you lease a coastline. I've looked into it. There's a form.
Out on the Antrim road, the Wardens finished their "road improvement works" and went to look at a crane.

then.text: Go on and sing with the lads. A song carries a yard better than a siren.
Nuala's at it again. Grand woman. Sit down till I tell you how a hull goes together.

A riveting squad was four lads. The heater boy kept the rivets glowing and threw them up. The catcher caught them in a bucket. The holder-on pressed the head, and the riveter hammered the other end flat.
Nobody asked the heater boy's name. He might have been fourteen. That's what Nuala wants written down, and I'll not argue.
Go and sing with the lads before you leave. Then read the plaque by the door. The 1907 one. That's the part they leave off the tea towels.

else.text: Nuala sent you? Then we'd better be properly introduced first. I'm usually about the streets of Belfast, near the cranes. Find me out there and bring a bowl of champ.

then.text: Dinner-hour songs, that's the yard. Fifty men and one tune, and not a note in common. Come back any time.

else.text: We sang on the way out of the gates, the whole shift at once. The tune's older than the yard. Give us a hand with the chorus.
Mervyn'll have my head if I sing before he's finished talking. Have a word with him first.
